observations: Two large head-like shapes in profile face each other against a near-black background, outlined in pale pink and lavender lines that trace jaw, crown, and chin edges.
Dense interior layers of purple, teal, yellow, red, and coral loops fill both forms, with repeated circular scribbles clustered where eye sockets and mouths would sit.
A coral-pink vertical shape descends between the two heads at center, its smooth curves contrasting with the tangled lines packed inside each form.
reading: Two hollow-looking heads lean toward each other, packed with overlapping color tangles that make their interiors feel restless and crowded. The coral link between them reads as a point of tension—shared breath or confrontation. The left head tilts slightly upward while the right one juts forward and down, giving the pair an uneven, off-balance quality that can feel like an argument caught mid-sentence.
contextAngle: In the owned Scrimshaw subset, this work sits between Scrimshaw 24 and Scrimshaw 40 by title number. Both neighbors show single heads; the doubled composition here stands out. Across the collection, the pairing of scrimshaw and nnxyz works highlights shared dense-line, dark-ground approaches to face-like forms.

connections.reason: Scrimshaw 24 fills a single head with similar purple and teal scribble density, but its lavender background and frontal stare contrast with the dark ground and paired profile format here.
Nifty faces #122 shares the black background and looping line clusters inside a rounded head form, but uses black outlines and a three-quarter view rather than colored-line profiles.

lookingQuestion: How does the smooth coral shape between the two heads change the way you read the space—does it connect the figures or separate them?
ambiguities: Whether the coral center form belongs to one head, both, or stands as an independent element is visually ambiguous.
The comparison to nifty faces #122 rests on shared line-and-dark-ground qualities; the two artists' works differ in outline weight and spatial depth.
